In Crime No.2918 Registered In The Kottiyam Police Station P10 True Copy Of The Representation Dated 3.11.2016 Preferred By The Petitioner Before The District Collector Respondent(S)' Exhibits Rasik S vs The State Of Kerala on 31 October, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112856336/ 2 ----------------------- Nil. / True Copy / P.S. texts.facts: P7 True Copy Of The Invoice No. 132, Dated 6.9.2016, Issued By The Msn Traders In Favour Of Parassery Trading Company Petitioner is a wholesale dealer in food-grains, doing business under the name and style 'Kottumala Traders'. According to the petitioner, petitioner is having necessary license, under the Food Safety and Standards Act and attendant Rules and Regulations. However on 31.10.2016, petitioner purchased wheat from another company, evident from Ext.P5 invoice. On 03.11.2016, out of the wheat purchased as per Ext.P5, petitioner sold wheat to another company in Kollam, as per Ext.P8 invoices. While the wheat being transported in lorry bearing registration No.KL-05-AB 1764, the same was intercepted by the Police, and took into custody the lorry as well as the product, alleging that the W.P.(C). NO. 36513 OF 2016 wheat transported are rationed articles. A crime was registered as Crime No. 2918 by the Kottiyam Police, alleging offences under Sections 3 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, read with Clause 5(A) of the Kerala Rationing Order, evident from Ext.P9 FIR. According to the petitioner, the wheat was purchased by the petitioner from outside agencies, which was sold by the Food Corporation of India to the dealer, and there is no manner of liability for the petitioner, as per the provisions of the Essential Commodities Act, and the Kerala Rationing Order. Therefore, there shall be a direction to release the wheat to the petitioner. The subject matter relates to an enquiry contemplated under Section 6A of the Essential Commodities Act.
